ent_principle_form_closure.name: Form Closure
ent_principle_form_closure.summary: A grasp condition in which the object's motion is completely constrained by the geometry and placement of frictionless contacts alone.
ent_principle_form_closure.body:
## Overview

Form Closure is a grasping condition that completely constrains the motion of an object solely through the geometry and arrangement of frictionless contacts. It does not rely on friction or active control; whether the object is fully locked is determined purely by the positions and normal directions of the contact points. What it truly changes is not the way grasping forces are applied, but rather the transformation of "grasping" from a force problem into a geometric one.

ent_principle_capture_point.name: Capture Point
ent_principle_capture_point.summary: A point on the ground where the robot must step to bring itself to a complete stop, used as a predictive balance criterion for bipedal walking.
ent_principle_capture_point.body:
## Overview

The Capture Point (CP) is a core concept in humanoid robot push recovery and gait planning: it is a point on the ground such that—if the robot can immediately step onto it and position its center of mass directly above the support foot—it can stop without needing to take another step [44][45]. The existence of the capture point transforms the complex dynamic balancing problem into a geometric question of "where to step next."

ent_principle_force_closure.name: Force Closure
ent_principle_force_closure.summary: A grasp condition in which arbitrary external wrench on the object can be balanced by contact forces without changing the contact configuration.
ent_principle_force_closure.body:
## Overview

Force Closure is a core criterion in grasp planning: under the condition that the contact configuration remains unchanged, contact forces can balance any external wrench applied to the object. What it truly changes is not "what poses the hand can make," but "the hand can still grasp objects under uncertainty"—from geometric contact feasibility to mechanical robust stability, it is the key leap from simulation to real-world grasping in grasp planning.
